entries.reason: the controller is the port's own and needs nothing the release lacks: a shared instance, and a record of which of the application's widgets have content, kept where the rest of the port keeps per-application state
entries.effect: +widgetController answers one shared controller for the process; -setHasContent:forWidgetWithBundleIdentifier: records the flag under the bundle identifier in NSUserDefaults, so the application reads back exactly what it wrote, and says once in the log that this release has no Notification Center and no widget host, so nothing ever asks a widget to refresh because of the record
entries.source: the headers of NCWidgetController.h in SDK 26.2 for the contract; iOS 6.1.3 has no Notification Center, no Today widgets and no widget host - there is nothing in its armv7 cache to hold one, read by objc.binary_inventory

entries.effect: one shared controller for the process, made on first call and the same one every time after
entries.source: the header of NCWidgetController.h in SDK 26.2

entries.reason: the record is real and readable; only the consumer is missing, and a consumer that is missing is the release's business, not something to fake
entries.effect: stores the flag for that bundle identifier in NSUserDefaults and synchronizes; an empty bundle identifier is ignored rather than turned into a key nothing can be read back with
entries.source: the header of NCWidgetController.h in SDK 26.2; the NSUserDefaults convention is the one UIApplication+UserNotificationSettings.m already uses for its own registered-types record

entries.reason: the factory that replaced the three named ones takes the style itself, and the port's UIVibrancyEffect is a real, comparable effect that keeps the style it was made with
entries.effect: a real UIVibrancyEffect carrying the given vibrancy style over the light material the widget is drawn with; it compares equal to another effect of the same style, archives and unarchives as the system's does, and -description names the style
entries.source: the headers of NCWidgetProviding.h in SDK 26.2 for the contract; the port's own UIVibrancyEffect (UIKit/UIVisualEffect.m) and +effectForBlurEffect:style: (UIKit/UIVibrancyEffect+Style13.m); the blur style values are read from UIBlurEffect.h in SDK 26.2 - ExtraLight 0, Light 1, Dark 2. NOT held against a host: the deprecation is ios(13.0, 14.0) and the host's UIKit declares none of these factories, measured by compiling a call to them for arm64-apple-ios15.0-macabi against the Command Line Tools' iOSSupport, which answers 'no known class method for selector'

entries.reason: the header's own words are 'for use with select supporting text and glyphs', which is the light material Notification Center is drawn with
entries.effect: a real UIVibrancyEffect over UIBlurEffectStyleLight, distinguishable from the secondary one by -isEqual: and by -description
entries.source: the header of NCWidgetProviding.h in SDK 26.2; the blur style values from UIBlurEffect.h in SDK 26.2. The mapping of the wording to the material is reasoned from that wording, not measured against a host - see facts/NotificationCenter/

entries.reason: the header's own words are 'where further diminution is required', one step lighter than the primary material, which is what ExtraLight is
entries.source: the header of NCWidgetProviding.h in SDK 26.2; the blur style values from UIBlurEffect.h in SDK 26.2. Reasoned from the wording, not measured against a host

entries.reason: the iOS 8 effect Notification Center drew itself with, and the same light material: iOS 10 replaced it with widgetEffectForVibrancyStyle:, whose primary style is that same material
entries.effect: a real UIVibrancyEffect over UIBlurEffectStyleLight, equal to the primary widget effect
entries.source: the header of NCWidgetProviding.h in SDK 26.2 (deprecated ios(8.0, 10.0) in favour of widgetEffectForVibrancyStyle:); the blur style values from UIBlurEffect.h in SDK 26.2. Reasoned, not measured against a host
